**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 7.7 (p0032)**

Section 7.7 requires *Customer* to pay Vendor "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" fifteen percent of the **annual** Fees for **each week** an invoice remains unpaid, triggered by a ten-day delay. This fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) and the fallback (a capped early-termination fee only), and is uncapped and compounding — walk-away territory, since it can exceed remaining contract value from a minor payment slip. Section 21.3 confirms payment obligations sit outside the liability cap, so nothing else constrains it.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: replace the LD with customary late-payment interest on **undisputed** invoices at the lesser of 1%/month or the legal maximum, running from written notice, plus an express statement that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer. Service credits and SLA remedies flowing to us were reviewed and left untouched.
